question: Why do I feel empty even when life is going well?
seo_title: Why Do I Feel Empty Even When Life Is Good? A Biblical Answer | TheWrkShop
description: Success, pleasure and attention can't fill a soul built for God. Why you can have everything and still feel hollow, and where real life is found, from Ecclesiastes 2:11.
answer: You can have success, pleasure, attention and good relationships and still feel restless and hollow, because the human soul was built for more than any of them can give. It was designed for union with God, and nothing else fully satisfies it. External abundance can't heal internal disconnection. Real life is found in reconnecting to the Source, not in adding more.

sections.heading: Ecclesiastes saw this thousands of years ago
paragraphs: Solomon had wealth, power, pleasure, wisdom, influence and achievement. He denied himself nothing. And his verdict was: "Everything was meaningless, a chasing after the wind."
Why? Because external abundance cannot heal internal disconnection. That's why people can have everything and still feel restless, anxious, lonely, disconnected and hollow.

sections.heading: Still breathing, but not truly alive
paragraphs: Most people think death begins physically. Biblically, it often begins on the inside. You see it when a man loses wonder, peace, tenderness, joy, purpose and his hunger for God. He becomes hardened, distracted, reactive, overstimulated and spiritually asleep. Still breathing, but not truly alive.

Paul wrote to people with a pulse, ambition and success and told them they had been "dead in your transgressions." A man can have all the markers of a good life and still be disconnected from true life.

sections.heading: Counterfeit life always fades
paragraphs: The enemy rarely tempts with obvious destruction first. He offers counterfeit aliveness: things that numb pain, excite emotions, inflate ego and distract the heart. But counterfeit life always fades, so you need more distraction, more noise, more validation and more stimulation to feel the same thing.
Jesus didn't call Himself a source of life. He said, "I am the life." A branch cut off from the vine eventually withers. Modern culture says independence is freedom. Jesus says connection is life.

scriptures.text: Yet when I surveyed all that my hands had done and what I had toiled to achieve, everything was meaningless, a chasing after the wind; nothing was gained under the sun.
My people have committed two sins: They have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and have dug their own cisterns, broken cisterns that cannot hold water.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy; I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.
You make known to me the path of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence, with eternal pleasures at your right hand.

steps: Name your "broken cisterns": the things you reach for when you feel empty, like your phone, work, food, drink, approval or entertainment.
For one week, notice the moment you reach for one. Pause and ask, "What am I actually hungry for right now?"
Start each morning with ten unhurried minutes with God before anything else gets your attention. Read Psalm 16 or John 15.
Take [What's Really First?](/tools/kingdom-first/) to see what's quietly governing your decisions and desires.

faqs.q: Is it wrong to feel empty when I have so much?
faqs.a: No. It's honest. That emptiness can be an invitation, a sign that you were made for more than what you've been filling your life with.

faqs.q: I'm a Christian. Why do I still feel empty?
faqs.a: Believers can drift into running on activity instead of connection with God. Jesus called it remaining in Him (John 15). Often the answer isn't doing more for God but spending real time with Him.

faqs.q: What if the emptiness won't lift?
faqs.a: Persistent emptiness, numbness or hopelessness can be signs of depression, which is real and treatable. Talk to your doctor or a licensed counselor. If you have thoughts of not wanting to live, call or text 988 in the US right away.
